# Huckleberry (01, engineer) — BAD-027

## Brief
Objective: On the admin dashboard's /accounts list, make the search box find an account by its @handle as well as its email, and add a `suspended` option to the status filter that lists the accounts whose profile is suspended, with a matching facet count. Show a `suspended` badge beside the @handle in the list so a suspended profile is visible in any view. Nothing else on the page changes.

Why: once my.badtakes.io/@handle is public, a report names a handle, not an email. Today `listAccounts` matches `a.account_email` only and its status filter is licence status (active/revoked), so an operator cannot find the account behind @handle or list suspended profiles. The 2026-08-20 profiles design's /profiles list (search by handle, active/suspended filter) was folded into /accounts without those two controls.

Behaviour, decided:
1. Search (`q`): trim, strip one leading `@`, lowercase (as today). Match `a.account_email like '%q%'` OR the handle. `private.profiles.handle` is citext; migration 0012 says why not to lean on citext's pattern matching, so compare `lower(pr.handle::text)` against the lowercased term. Keep the existing unescaped `like` behaviour for `%` and `_`; do not widen scope there.
2. One where clause, two queries. `countAccounts` (the empty-page fallback) has no PROFILE_JOIN today and repeats the predicates by hand; a handle-only search past the end would count wrong. Factor the where clause into one exported-or-module constant used by both `listAccounts` and `countAccounts`, and give `countAccounts` the profile join it now needs.
3. Status: widen `AccountsQuery.status` to `LicenseStatus | 'suspended' | 'all'`. `suspended` means `pr.suspended_at is not null`; `active`/`revoked` stay licence status. `admin/src/app/accounts/page.tsx` maps `statusParam === 'suspended'` through.
4. Facets: `accountFacets` gains `suspended`: the number of accounts in `acct` whose profile has `suspended_at is not null` (same join key as PROFILE_JOIN, `pr.email = a.account_email`), computed inside the same single query so it stays one round trip, and so the chip's number equals the filter's total.
5. `admin/src/components/AccountFilters.tsx`: placeholder "Search by email or @handle…", aria-label "Search accounts by email or handle"; the status select gains `<option value="suspended">Suspended ({facets.suspended})</option>`. Suspended is a profile state, not a licence state: two `<optgroup>`s (Licence: Active, Revoked; Profile: Suspended) are welcome, your call on the markup. The `facets` prop type gains `suspended: number`.
6. List row: add `pr.suspended_at as profile_suspended_at` to PROFILE_COLUMNS, `profileSuspendedAt: string | null` on `AccountRow` (filled in `accountFrom` with `iso(...)`), and in page.tsx render `<span className="badge revoked">suspended</span>` next to the @handle when set, the badge the detail page already uses for a suspended profile. PROFILE_COLUMNS is also read by the detail query further down accounts.ts; check that mapper still compiles.
7. Test: add `test/server/admin-accounts-list.test.mjs` in the shape of `test/server/admin-moderation.test.mjs` (text assertions over admin source, because admin is TypeScript and this repo's runner is `node --test` over plain JS). Pin: the list and count queries share one where-clause constant; that clause names both `account_email` and `handle`; `countAccounts` joins `private.profiles`; page.tsx accepts `suspended` for status; AccountFilters offers `value="suspended"`; `accountFacets` counts `suspended`. `test/server/admin-pool.test.mjs` must stay green: no `Promise.all`/`allSettled`/`race`/`any` or bare `.map(async …)` under admin/src, ever (admin/CLAUDE.md: the pool is three connections behind a transaction pooler and a fan-out wedges the page).

Setup: this is a fresh worktree. Run `bash scripts/worktree-init.sh` first, from the worktree root. Then `cd admin && npm ci` if `admin/node_modules` is missing (admin has its own package-lock).

Verification (the project's `implementing-changes` skill applies; admin has no smoke leg, so this is what `.github/workflows/admin-ci.yml` runs):
- from `admin/`: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` — all three green, quote the tail of each.
- from the repo root: `node --test test/server/admin-*.test.mjs` — every admin test including the new one green; then `npm test` for the whole suite (pack tests skip without voicepacks/ — say so, do not claim they ran).
- live proof, preferred: `podman ps` shows the local Supabase stack when it is up (never start it, one stack serves every worktree; never Docker Desktop or OrbStack). If it is up, `admin/README.md` § local development names the `LICENSING_DB_URL`, `npm run seed` (writes nine `@seed.badtakes.test` accounts, idempotent) and `npm run dev` on port 3200; load `/accounts?q=<a seeded handle>` and `/accounts?status=suspended` and quote what the page returned (the sign-in path is `npm run dev:code`). If the stack is down or sign-in blocks you, say so in the return and rely on the build and tests; do not spend more than a few minutes on it.

Done when: the seven behaviours above are implemented, the new test file exists and passes, typecheck/lint/build are green on the exact tree you leave behind, `member log` records progress and `member result` records what you built with the verification output quoted.

CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF, worth Spud knowing: behaviour 1 said trim, strip one leading @, lowercase 'as today'. The @ strip was NOT there. listAccounts did only trim() then toLowerCase(). I added a replace of a leading @ between them: only the first, only at the front, because @ is legal inside an email address. Without it the new placeholder's promise would be false and a pasted @handle would match nothing, since migration 0012 constrains the stored handle to lowercase word characters only.
